the holy district set apart for the LORD, breadth
measurements.notes: ESV follows the Septuagint ('20,000'); the Hebrew reads 10,000 in all three places (ESV footnotes at 45:1, 48:9 ['Compare 45:1'], and 48:13). With 10,000 the district is the priests' strip alone (48:10); with 20,000 it is the priests' + Levites' strips together (48:10-13), which 48:20's 25,000-square total (20,000 + the 5,000 city strip) supports. Both readings preserved; rendered per the ESV as printed.

measurements.subject: the holy district set apart for the LORD, length
measurements.notes: The ESV's measure footnote at 45:1/48:8 glosses both the common and the long cubit; recorded as the long cubit per the vision's own declared standard (Ezek 40:5), the convention used across the Ezekiel 40-48 dataset.

measurements.subject: the whole set-apart portion (holy district together with the property of the city), square
measurements.notes: 48:8 gives the full strip's 25,000-cubit breadth; 48:20 squares it: the 20,000-broad holy district plus the 5,000-broad property of the city.

measurements.subject: the Levites' allotment, breadth
measurements.notes: ESV follows the Septuagint at 45:5 for the holding's use ('as their possession for cities to live in'; Hebrew 'as their possession, twenty chambers' - ESV footnote).

measurements.subject: the Levites' allotment, length
the city, each dimension (its length, width, and height are equal)
measurements.notes: The city lies foursquare; he measured it with the rod at 12,000 stadia, and 'its length and width and height are equal' (21:16). Recorded per dimension, the plain reading of the equality clause; a minority reading takes 12,000 as the total perimeter (3,000 per side). ESV footnote: 'About 1,380 miles; a stadion was about 607 feet.' Whether the equal height makes a cube or a pyramid the text does not say — a form question for the render, not this record (the engine's terraced massing is a documented decision, RENDERING-DECISIONS entry #2).

measurements.subject: the wall of the city, measured by the angel
measurements.notes: 'He also measured its wall, 144 cubits by human measurement, which is also an angel's measurement' (21:17). The text does not say WHICH dimension: recorded as height after 21:12's 'a great, high wall', but many interpreters read thickness (a wall-section measure) — hence tier `fuzzy`; the referent is underdetermined, the number is not. ESV footnote: 'About 216 feet; a cubit was about 18 inches' — the common cubit, not Ezekiel's long cubit (Ezek 40:5 does not govern John's vision).

measurements.subject: the priests' allotment (the sanctuary section), breadth
measurements.notes: 10,000 cubits on the western and on the eastern side (48:10). The portion is a place for the priests' houses and a holy place for the sanctuary (45:4).

measurements.subject: the priests' allotment (the sanctuary section), length
measurements.notes: Measured on the northern and southern sides (48:10), with the sanctuary of the LORD in its midst.
